messages:
ana: heads up — after the merge of PR #4028 i'm seeing a clear p95 jump on decode for short-seq workloads. baseline ~40ms, canary ~115ms.

matt: saw that too on the canary dashboard. looks correlated with the prefetch heuristic tweak that went in yesterday.

kavya: which tweak exactly? i only skimmed the PR, thought it was a small reorder in prefetch logic.

ana: the PR bumped the eager prefetch threshold and changed the eviction tie-breaker. snippet from canary trace: 

```
// runtime config (changed in PR 4028)
prefetch.enabled = true
prefetch.kv_prefetch_ratio = 0.9   // was 0.6
prefetch.eviction_policy = "age_then_size" // used to be "size_then_age"
```

ana: (typo above, that was me)

cheng: nvprof on a repro run shows attention kernel memcpy host->device increased by ~3x for short sequences; also observed more kernel launches (small matmuls) instead of fused matmul+attention. looks like prefetching more KV pages is causing more small op invocations.

sam: could be the scheduling boundary — if prefetching forces KV warmups mid-decode we might lose fused-op locality and hit kernel-choice fallback. have traces?

ana: pasted a condensed perf sample from canary run: 
```
p50 decode: 18ms -> 20ms
p95 decode: 42ms -> 118ms
tokens/sec: 1.8k -> 1.3k
gpu memcpy HtoD (sum): +320MB/s
attention_matmul kernel time: +2.4x
fused_attn_invocations: 1200 -> 380
```

matt: wow fused_attn drop is telling. PR probably introduced more asynchronous prefetch calls that break batching/fusion windows.

kavya: does the config change set prefetch to happen earlier (longer lookahead)? that could cause more prefix KV populating and change micro-batching behavior.

cheng: checked logs: prefetch now triggers at token_index >= 1 instead of >= 4 for short sequences. that means we kick off prefetch for nearly every request. aggregate effect: prefetches interleave with decode kernels.

sam: suggested triage: 1) reproduce locally with the tiny-runner harness, 2) run nvprof with concurrent kernel timeline, 3) rollback the prefetech ratio change in staging, 4) add a metric guard to avoid prefetching for seq_len < 8.

ana: i reproduced with tiny-runner. attached flame output (cropped): prefetch memcpy spikes between decode tokens 0..6, causing eviction and extra kernel-launch overhead.

deploy-bot: deploy 4028 applied to canary at 2026-03-17T21:04Z by matt.

matt: i'm going to open a revert PR for the prefetch ratio change and add a shortseq guard. will run canary.

kavya: before revert, can we try a patch that keeps threshold=0.9 but disables prefetch for seq_len < 8? cheaper to test.

cheng: i pushed a quick branch `prefetch-shortseq-guard` with the conditional. nvprof locally shows fused_attn invocations back up to ~1100 (vs 380). p95 dropped to ~48ms.

ana: great. can we run a perf CI with that branch? if green, promote as hotfix instead of full revert.

matt: launching perf CI now. job: perf-decode-shortseq-2026-03-17.

deploy-bot: perf CI job started: perf-decode-shortseq-2026-03-17 (job id 88922).

sam: if perf CI passes, plan: merge guard patch -> promote to canary -> monitor 1 hour -> rollout. if fails, full revert of PR 4028. also add an automated test that asserts fused_attn_invocations drop no more than 10% on shortseq.

kavya: i'll own adding the test. ana, can you draft the canary monitoring dashboard widgets we need? specifically fused_attn_invocations, memcpy HtoD rate, p95 decode, tokens/sec.

ana: on it. will post dashboard links once done.

matt: thanks all. priority: restore shortseq p95. update here with perf CI result.

deploy-bot: perf CI job completed: job id 88922 — status: SUCCESS — p95 improved to 49ms on patch branch.

matt: merging guard patch to main and promoting to canary. will keep canary frozen for 2h and watch metrics.

sam: follow-up action items: (1) add regression test for prefetch/kernels (kavya), (2) add metric guard in config to default disable aggressive prefetch on small sequences (matt), (3) re-evaluate eviction tie-breaker logic - it might still cause unnecessary evictions (cheng).

ana: logging this as rollout-blocker->resolved for now, will reopen if we see spikes after canary promotion. :thumbsup:
